title: Sentencing Guidelines — Murder contrary to s.203 Penal Code
summary: Starting point ranges for murder considering aggravating and mitigating factors. Post-Francis Muruatetu jurisprudence requires individualised sentencing; death penalty not mandatory.
guideline: Consider age, role, weapon, premeditation, victim impact, mitigation and remorse.

title: Sentencing Guidelines — Robbery with violence s.296(2)
summary: Guidance on capital robbery: use of weapons, gang membership, injury to victims. Courts must weigh culpability after Muruatetu principles.
guideline: Record aggravating factors on the face of the sentence; consider plea and restitution.

title: Sentencing Guidelines — Sexual offences
summary: Age of victim, violence, infection with disease, and relationship to victim are key factors. Minimum sentences subject to constitutional challenge jurisprudence.
guideline: Primary consideration: age of complainant and harm caused.

title: Sentencing Guidelines — Narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances
statute: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Control) Act
summary: Quantity, role (trafficker vs user), and previous record guide sentence. Harm-reduction considerations for users.
guideline: Differentiate traffickers from addicts; treatment options for users.

title: Sentencing Guidelines — Theft and stealing by servant
summary: Value of property, breach of trust, restitution and mitigation affect sentence. Corporate theft may attract higher terms.
guideline: Record value stolen and whether restitution has been made.

title: Sentencing Guidelines — Causing death by dangerous driving
summary: Speed, intoxication, prior convictions, and victim impact guide sentencing. Restorative options available in some cases.
guideline: Distinguish momentary inattention from prolonged recklessness.

title: Sentencing Guidelines — Corruption and economic crimes
summary: Amount involved, public office held, recovery of proceeds and cooperation with investigators are relevant factors.
guideline: Aim at deterrence and recovery of public funds.

title: Sentencing Guidelines — Child justice
summary: Detention is a last resort. Community-based sentences, probation and restorative justice preferred.
guideline: Best interests of the child paramount.
